hooks.text: A cosmic behemoth weighing three quadrillion Suns is tearing itself apart.
The universe's heaviest distant giant is not a single peaceful object.
Three quadrillion solar masses are colliding at millions of kilometers per hour.

title: The Cosmic Giant Tearing Itself Apart
description: Astronomers discovered El Gordo, a titan weighing up to three quadrillion Suns. Instead of one peaceful cluster, it is two massive systems smashing together at extreme speeds.

beats.text: A cosmic behemoth weighing three quadrillion Suns is tearing itself apart.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope and Chandra X-ray composite of galaxy cluster El Gordo, 2014

beats.text: Many people imagine the universe's heaviest distant galaxy cluster is a single, peaceful object.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope deep view of massive galaxy cluster Abell 1689, 2003

beats.text: In 2012, astronomers analyzed an extreme giant nicknamed El Gordo, Spanish for 'The Fat One'.
beats.visual: Night sky photograph of the constellation Phoenix over the Atacama Desert, 2018

beats.text: This titan in the Phoenix constellation produces the most X-rays of any known distant cluster.
beats.visual: Chandra X-ray Observatory false-color X-ray image of El Gordo, 2012

beats.text: But data reveals El Gordo is actually two separate subclusters colliding at millions of kilometers per hour.
beats.visual: Numerical simulation showing two galaxy cluster subclusters colliding, 2012

beats.text: The impact is so violent that hot gas was wrenched away from unseen dark matter.
beats.visual: Chandra and Hubble composite of the Bullet Cluster showing gas separated from dark matter, 2006

beats.text: Its massive weight warps spacetime, creating a magnifying glass that bends light from background galaxies.
beats.visual: James Webb Space Telescope infrared view showing gravitationally lensed background galaxies behind El Gordo, 2023
queries: El Gordo galaxy cluster Webb infrared

beats.text: Instead of a single giant, we find that the heaviest distant clusters are actually catastrophic collisions.
beats.visual: Wide field composite view of galaxy cluster El Gordo, 2014

better_than_last: Refined the concluding beat to emphasize the reviewer's requested discovery shift while maintaining a tight loop back to the initial destruction imagery.
